title: Smooth locus and geometric lifts in an etale nodal model
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a flat locally finitely presented morphism of schemes [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-pc-scheme]. Let $b:V\to Y$ and $q:U\to X$ be etale morphisms [def-weil-etale-morphism], and let $p:U\to V$ satisfy $f\circ q=b\circ p$. Suppose $h\in\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$ and an etale $V$-morphism $e:U\to W=\operatorname{Spec}_V(\mathcal O_V[u,v]/(uv-h))$ are given; the relative spectrum denotes the scheme obtained by gluing the indicated affine spectra [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Put $N=V(u,v)\subset W$, the closed subscheme defined by the two coordinate functions [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The projection identifies $N$ with the zero subscheme $V(h)\subset V$. For every $t\in U$, the following are equivalent: $f$ is nonsmooth at $q(t)$, $p$ is nonsmooth at $t$, $W\to V$ is nonsmooth at $e(t)$, and $e(t)\in N$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. For every geometric point $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ [def-weil-geometric-point] and every $t\in U$ over its image, there is a lift $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U$ over $\bar x$ with image $t$. If $f$ is nonsmooth at $\bar x$, this lift maps into $N$.

source.place: Tag 01V9, lemma-smooth-at-point (fibre/differential criterion, applied to uv-h); descent.tex Tag 02KM, lemma-syntomic-smooth-etale-permanence; morphisms.tex Tag 02GL, lemma-etale-over-field.

proof.text: Work over an affine open $V_0=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset V$, writing $h$ also for its restriction and $B=R[u,v]/(uv-h)$. By [def-weil-closed-immersion] and [def-weil-affine-spectrum], the restriction of $N$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(B/(u,v))$. Evaluation at $u=v=0$ gives $B/(u,v)=R/(h)$: the relation $uv-h$ becomes $-h$, and the inverse sends the class of $r$ to its constant class. These maps commute with restriction to smaller affine opens, so glue to the asserted isomorphism $N\simeq V(h)$ over $V$.

source.place: Tag 01V9, lemma-smooth-at-point: elementary affine preparation for uv-h; quotient calculation.

proof.text: On $D(u)\subset\operatorname{Spec}B$, use the presentation $B[1/u]=R[v,w,u]/(uv-h,uw-1)$. The Jacobian minor in the first two variables $v,w$ is $\operatorname{diag}(u,u)$, with determinant $u^2$, a unit since $uw=1$. Thus this is a standard smooth presentation by [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra], and its ring map is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-is-smooth]. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine] its spectrum is smooth over $V_0$. The identification with $D(u)$ is the principal-localization open immersion of [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion]. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes] this gives smoothness at every point of $D(u)$ for $W\to V$. Exchanging $u,v$ gives the same result on $D(v)$. Hence $W\to V$ is smooth outside $N$.

source.place: Tags 00T6, definition-standard-smooth, and 00T7, lemma-standard-smooth (1); explicit 2 by 2 minor.

proof.text: Fix $w\in N$ over $V_0$, and put $k=\kappa(w)$. The residue map $R\to k$ kills $h$. Set $D=k[a,b]/(a^2,b^2)$, $I=(ab)\subset D$ and $E=D/I$. The monomials $1,a,b,ab$ are a $k$-basis of $D$, so $ab\ne0$ and $I^2=0$. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}E\subset\operatorname{Spec}D$ is a first order thickening by [def-sbc-first-order-thickening]. Give $D,E$ their $R$-structures through $k$ and define $B\to E$ by $u\mapsto a$, $v\mapsto b$. This is well-defined since $ab=0$ in $E$. Both spectra have a single point, and the resulting map to $W$ has image $w$ (its residue map is the chosen $B\to k$). Any lift over $R$ would send $u$ to $a+\lambda ab$ and $v$ to $b+\mu ab$ for $\lambda,\mu\in k$. Their product is $ab\ne0$, whereas the image of $h$ is zero. Therefore no lift exists. If $W\to V$ were smooth on an open neighbourhood $O$ of $w$, [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme] would factor $\operatorname{Spec}E\to W$ through $O$. Any lift would still have image $w$, hence factor through the affine model by the same open-factorization lemma, giving the impossible ring lift just calculated. Smoothness implies formal smoothness by [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], contradicting the lifting requirement of [def-sbc-formally-smooth]. Thus every point of $N$ is nonsmooth. Together with step 2 this proves the model's precise smooth locus.

source.place: Tag 02H0, definition-formally-smooth; explicit square-zero obstruction for uv=0 at the origin, written by Q51.

proof.text: Fix $t\in U$. Suppose $f$ is smooth at $q(t)$ and choose an open smooth neighbourhood $X_0$. Put $U_0=q^{-1}(X_0)$. The maps $U_0\to X_0$ and $b:V\to Y$ are etale: open restrictions preserve etaleness by clauses (1)--(3) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. Apply the commutative-square conclusion of [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties] with $P=$ smooth to $X_0\to Y$, $U_0\to X_0$, $V\to Y$, and $p|_{U_0}$. It says $p|_{U_0}$ is smooth. Conversely, if $p$ is smooth on an open $O$ containing $t$, the same cited lemma, with $a=\mathrm{id}_O$, says that $b\circ p|_O$ is smooth (the postcomposition case of its locality assertion). Since $b\circ p=f\circ q$, [lem-trf-etale-source-smoothness], in its pointwise form applied to $q$, implies $f$ is smooth at $q(t)$. This proves $f$ smooth at $q(t)\Longleftrightarrow p$ smooth at $t$. Applying that pointwise source lemma to the etale map $e:U\to W$ over $V$ gives $p$ smooth at $t\Longleftrightarrow W\to V$ smooth at $e(t)$. Negating these equivalences and using steps 2--3 proves all four nonsmoothness equivalences.

source.place: Tags 04QZ, definition-local-source-target; 04R1, lemma-local-source-target-characterize; 04R3, remark-list-local-source-target (smooth); source locality Tag 036U.

proof.text: For the prescribed $\bar x$ and $t$, apply the last, prescribed-point clause of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-cover-geometric-point-lift] to the jointly surjective family $\{q:U\to X,\mathrm{id}_X:X\to X\}$, selecting its member $q$ and the given point $t$. The identity is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (it is an open immersion). The clause supplies $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U$ with $q\bar t=\bar x$ and image exactly $t$, with the original field $\Omega$. If $f$ is nonsmooth at $\bar x$, step 4 gives $e(t)\in N$. The composite geometric point $e\bar t$ factors scheme-theoretically through $N$: in an affine model, $u,v$ have zero residue at $e(t)$, hence map to zero in $\Omega$, so its ring map kills $(u,v)$. This is the closed-subscheme quotient description of [def-weil-closed-immersion].
